rationales: Experimentation tests a proposed explanation and comes after initial observation.
A hypothesis is formulated after observing a biological problem.
Observation is the first step in solving a biological problem.
Deduction follows from a hypothesis and is not the first step.
Monera are prokaryotes and lack a nuclear envelope.
Protista are eukaryotes and have a nuclear envelope.
Fungi are eukaryotes and have a nuclear envelope.
Plants are eukaryotes and have a nuclear envelope.
Cellulose is a major component of plant cell walls, not prokaryotic walls.
Peptidoglycan is the main structural material in most prokaryotic cell walls.
Chitin is found in fungal cell walls.
Plasmodesmata are channels between plant cells, not cell-wall material.
Chromosomes consist of DNA associated with proteins.
Lipids are not the principal components of chromosomes.
DNA is a chromosome component, but chromosomes also contain proteins.
RNA is not the principal material of chromosomes.
Mitochondria contain their own DNA.
Golgi bodies do not have their own DNA.
Vacuoles do not have their own DNA.
Centrioles do not have their own DNA.
Osmosis is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane, not movement of molecules against a concentration gradient.
Active transport moves substances from lower to higher concentration using energy.
Diffusion is movement from higher to lower concentration.
Filtration is movement driven by pressure.
Ernst Haeckel proposed a three-kingdom system, but did not introduce the earliest classification system.
Carolus Linnaeus developed a formal classification system later in history.
Aristotle introduced an early system for classifying organisms.
Robert Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification much later.
Homo sapiens is the scientific name of humans.
Pisum sativum is the scientific name of pea.
Rosa indica is a rose name, not the scientific name of humans.
Allium cepa is the scientific name of onion.
Cedrus bark is not the traditional source of an effective malaria treatment.
Cinchona bark contains quinine, which was used to treat malaria.
Pinus bark is not the traditional source of quinine.
Cactus bark is not used as the traditional malaria remedy.
Aluminium is not generally listed among the principal bioelements in this context.
Cobalt can occur as a trace element, but it is not the expected principal bioelement here.
Bromine is not one of the principal bioelements.
Carbon is a major bioelement found in organic compounds.
The right atrium receives blood and is not the strongest chamber.
The left atrium receives blood and is not the strongest chamber.
The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs and is less muscular than the left ventricle.
The left ventricle is the strongest chamber because it pumps blood throughout the body.
The renal artery carries oxygenated blood to the kidneys.
The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.
The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.
The aorta carries oxygenated blood from the heart to the body.
Ingestion is taking food into the body.
Absorption is the uptake of digested nutrients.
Defecation is the elimination of undigested food from the body.
Digestion is the breakdown of food into simpler substances.
Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm.
The later stages of aerobic respiration occur in mitochondria, but glycolysis does not.
The nucleus is not where glycolysis occurs.
The endoplasmic reticulum is not where glycolysis occurs.
Emil Fischer proposed the lock-and-key model, not the induced-fit model.
Daniel Koshland proposed the induced-fit model.
Robert Hooke is known for observing and naming cells, not proposing this model.
Theodor Schwann contributed to cell theory, not the induced-fit model.
